Title: The reason why players are leaving the game

Messages.Author: Stefan Ferenci
Messages.Body:
first off: gehennas events are an annoyance that should not have been
printed, but with the exception of a few (e.g.:recalled to the founder,
nightmares upon nightmares, the unmasking) they won´t see much tourney
play and in the long run won´t affect Vtes. recalled to the founder is a
real pain in the ass and mostly benefits weenies, a decktyp that is in
whatever form (bleed, vote, combat, intercept) one of the strongest in
this game. (although most cam+antitribu hybrid decks aren´t affect as
well) and even if you will never manage to build a working deck that can
play recalled to the founder regularly. if some wacky guys at your table
decides to play one (just for fun) it will ruin your game if you play
mono clan.
but i think gehenna is not the reason why people are leaving the game.
the reason is the lack of change in vtes. tourneys are still dominated
by stealth bleed. almost every major tournament sees at least one !malk
deck and another S&B deck in the final. combat decks are almost a
nonfactor in tourney vtes (with the exception of the eurobrujah deck)
and non weenie vote decks that do not include the big 2 (arika, leandro)
are rarly successfull. showing up at a tourney without intercept and/or
bounce will result in you being called mr. bleed sink (i played a deck
that couldn´t bounce at the hungarian qualifier and i ate an horrible
amount of deflected bleeds)
the last 3 expansions brought only new stuff that either people would
like to play, but that is simply to weak (anarchism and black hand) or
stuff that adds an unnessary amount of luck and randomness to the game
(gehenna events)
vampires with a capacity above 8 are most of the time wallpaper
(especially if they have no real title (bishop/primogen doesn´t count))
there is NO benefit in playing larger vampires except if the have cool
specials and disciplines (like the ic´s or laz).
some changes have been proposed (i suggest to LSJ at the ec that the
biggies might need some sort of supersuperior (playable by vampires with
a capacity above 7/8 if they have no title), just to be told that large
vampires are strong enough)
maybe vampires should only be allowed to bleed to a maximum of half
their capacity
maybe vampires should get +1 strengh when in combat with a younger vampire
a lot of people are pissed the way the bloodlones are treated (no more
group 2 vamps, some of them totally unplayable) the average CCG player
DOESN`T care how many samedi are found in the world of darkness!
i appreciate that WW has been carefull about not destroying the game,
but the stasis the game is currently in might destroy the game.
please no flames as a reply

stefan

are a pain in the ass and can be frustrating as hell.

> but i think gehenna is not the reason why people are leaving the game.

There has to be an easiest way to win. Note that with proper
preprations SB isn't necessarily going to win any games. But, every

should be SB, as it is the most sincere deck type.

Competitiveness-wise, you may be right.

I must confess though that I derive special pleasure in sweeping a
table with decks like Assamite (D) Rush combat especially because the

myself playing nonstandard decks even at tourneys.

> there is NO benefit in playing larger vampires except if the have cool

Sadly, this is really the case. To play a fattie you usually need at
least two of the following: 1. multiple action ability, 2. very cool
special, 3. über discipline spread, 4. 3 or more votes. Few things
shorter would warrant it. Especially (caution, proceed at your own
risk) since they are way too easy to burn.

> biggies might need some sort of supersuperior (playable by vampires with
> a capacity above 7/8 if they have no title), just to be told that large
> vampires are strong enough)

I must confess that I am somewhat in disagreement with the current
crypt card design formula. I think that at least two articles are
underrated (titles and +1 Intercept). I'm not sure though that the
vampires should gain any more points' worth of abilities, but some
more cards like Aranthebes could still be welcome.

> maybe vampires should only be allowed to bleed to a maximum of half their capacity
> maybe vampires should get +1 strengh when in combat with a younger vampire

Actually, stuff like these would make excellent Events (even if they
would not be cool Gehenna cards). It is quite possible to use the new
mechanic to favor the fatties.

> a lot of people are pissed the way the bloodlones are treated (no more

I'm probably the minority here, but I like the bloodlines _because_
they are hard to play. I'm currently going mono-True Brujah... ;)

> i appreciate that WW has been carefull about not destroying the game,
> but the stasis the game is currently in might destroy the game.

Stasis is one thing. Slow change is another. I'm not sure whether I
like the new pro-Combat deck mechanisms like Carver's and Lilith
(making combat decks win easier) because part of the challenge will be
gone. But then again, I'm one of those guys who was regularly playing
Gangrel Antitribu before SW... ;) (Read - probably masochistic beyond
redemption when it comes to a choice of decks.)

Bye,

Daneel

play non-camarilla, for instance).

something too big, but I'm not sure.

Gehenna cards are definitely not worth bothering in the long run (with the
noted exceptions), but the concept of Event-cards in general I consider to
be cool. I think that Gehenna events are merely a big field test in order to
make the player community ready for more such cards to come (Event cards,
not Gehenna events, that is).

> but i think gehenna is not the reason why people are leaving the game.
> the reason is the lack of change in vtes. tourneys are still dominated

> like to play, but that is simply to weak (anarchism and black hand) or
> stuff that adds an unnessary amount of luck and randomness to the game
> (gehenna events)

I concede that White Wolf's design team follows a very cautious strategy
regarding card design, which is also backed up by the army of playtesters
who immediately call out if a card shows only the faintest hint to be
breakable. If you scan the list of cards in tournament winning decks, more
often than not more than 90% of the library is made out of cards first
published in one of the old sets. Only very few new cards make it into
tournament calibre decks and if they do, they are most likely to be Masters
(eg Zillah's Valley). Slightly bigger cojones might be perfectly OK when
designing new cards.

On the other hand the three big strategies (bleed, vote, combat) tower above
us as the only three available strategies under the current victory
conditions. As long as the changes to the game mechanics are not more
drastic, people will usually look for cards that either directly hurt other
players (bleed enhancers, damage votes), crush other minions (cool combat
cards or votes) or make the minions easier/harder to block.

BTW: What I *really* like is the change in the philosophy about which cards
are common and rare. The recent sets feature mostly (unique) Master cards or
unique permanents. This is something I would like to positively point out,
because it makes it far easier for the players to build playable decks with
new cards without investing a fortune just to get enough copies of staple
cards (anyone still hunting Shroud of Absence?) and you usually don't need
more than one or two copies of most rare cards.

> vampires with a capacity above 8 are most of the time wallpaper
> (especially if they have no real title (bishop/primogen doesn´t count))
> there is NO benefit in playing larger vampires except if the have cool
> specials and disciplines (like the ic´s or laz).

If you refer to torunament dacks, yes. In casual play - and this makes the
vast majority of games I play - you see a much broarder variety of decks
with more wacky strategies. I know this is quite insatisfactory for you,
because I know you as a very achievement-oriented player for who the
second-best option does not make the cut. But the diesign team can't
exclusively design cards with tournament play in mind. We will never see a
set entirely made out of tournament-calibre cards (and I am quite happy
about it), for this would mean that most cards would read either "+bleed",
"+stealth" or "+intercept". And who is eager to see the umpteenth variety of
a DOM bleed card?

> some changes have been proposed [snip the propositions]

> i appreciate that WW has been carefull about not destroying the game,
> but the stasis the game is currently in might destroy the game.

Your propositions are all worth considering. What I like about them is that
you do not propose hoser cards against certain strategies, but that you try
to shift the balance with the means currently available to the game. Wether
a vampire should bleed for half it's capacity or for one-third or one-(add
your favorite number here, but PLEASE, no discussion about this) is not the
point here.

But I agree that if a certain facette of the game (in this case: most big
vampires) doesn't see play outside casual games, some changes should be up
for discussion.

Best regards,
Sascha Neumayr

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
Stefan Ferenci <a950n...@unet.s.p.a.m.univie.ac.at> wrote in message news:<40b34a28$0$8840$3b21...@usenet.univie.ac.at>...

> printed, but with the exception of a few (e.g.:recalled to the founder,
> nightmares upon nightmares, the unmasking) they won´t see much tourney
> play and in the long run won´t affect Vtes.

I think this is WAY WAY WAY too early to make such an absolute
statement, considering none of the cards are remotely tourney-legal
yet. I'm very curious to see how Events _actually_ filter into
tournament play compared to people's wild-guess expectations.

> recalled to the founder is a
> real pain in the ass and mostly benefits weenies, a decktyp that is in
> whatever form (bleed, vote, combat, intercept) one of the strongest in
> this game. (although most cam+antitribu hybrid decks aren´t affect as
> well) and even if you will never manage to build a working deck that can
> play recalled to the founder regularly. if some wacky guys at your table
> decides to play one (just for fun) it will ruin your game if you play
> mono clan.

Of course, you won't ever see someone playing 'one (just for fun)',
since it requires two OTHER events to be in play and reduces the hand
size by one for the duration of its effect. You'll pretty much _have_
to be facing someone who specifically plans to use this event as part
of his strategy.

That said, it may well 'ruin your game' if you play mono-clan and you
do not have a vampire of sufficient size (a whopping 6-cap!) to lose
to grant yourself immunity to RttF. Of course, the guy who plays a PTO
'just for fun' from his Cam-vote deck can also ruin your game - or the
guy who plays with one Judgment: Camarilla Segregation because he's
playing an all-Cam deck... or even the guy who diabs your torpored
vamp just because he can get away with it.

Of course, if your predator or prey chooses to play one and it hoses
you, it's no longer 'just for fun' but also a potentially useful
strategy move.

But there are lots and lots and lots of cards and plays that can
totally screw someone cross-table if a player is doing things 'just
for fun'. That can certainly discourage people who are trying to play
more seriously, and that disparity (the 'wacky fun' player vs. a
serious player) gets talked about a lot in terms of 'new players in
their first tourney that might totally unbalance a game'. If you've
got a player who might totally screw you across table 'for fun' or
otherwise unwittingly, it might be worth pointing out that his idea of
'fun' includes ruining your own enjoyment, thus reducing the chance
that you'll be that interested in playing with them again. Take a
minute and talk to them about why wacky cross-table-screw plays don't
help them win.

There are plenty of people who play together to have fun and don't
care about winning; nothing inherently wrong with that as long as it's
understood by all involved that playing seriously with the
primary/sole objective to win isn't the goal of the players.

> but i think gehenna is not the reason why people are leaving the game.
> the reason is the lack of change in vtes. tourneys are still dominated
> by stealth bleed. almost every major tournament sees at least one !malk
> deck and another S&B deck in the final.

Coincidentally enough the last several tourneys I have been at
(including a Regional Qualifier) have seen neither stealth-bleed nor
!Malks doing well - the Qualifier had neither at the final table. But
I know other major tourneys see plenty of both (case in point, the
recent German championship) lately, so it's in part a matter of local
environment. My recent environment has seen a predominance of
mega-intercept and Camarilla-big-cap vote decks; yours is as you
state.

> Combat decks are almost a

> nonfactor in tourney vtes (with the exception of the eurobrujah deck)
> and non weenie vote decks that do not include the big 2 (arika, leandro)
> are rarly successfull.

Combat looks to be getting a big boost from Gehenna, with things like
the Path of Lilith, Dragonbound, and other forward-motion combat
cards. At least, I'd like to see it be more played at a tourney level,
personally.

> showing up at a tourney without intercept and/or
> bounce will result in you being called mr. bleed sink (i played a deck
> that couldn´t bounce at the hungarian qualifier and i ate an horrible
> amount of deflected bleeds)

You're absolutely right: playing a deck with no ability to stop
yourself from being bled with even a minimum of stealth (since you're
'without intercept) will make you a bleed sink.

However, more of a problem for such a deck than being given a
derogatory name like 'bleed sink' is that it probably loses most
games, as you're neglecting to have a way to counter one of the most
basic of ways your predator might oust you. (Unless you're playing
with a non-intercept non-bounce answer like massive bleed reduction,
in which case you don't care about being a sink.)

> the last 3 expansions brought only new stuff that either people would
> like to play, but that is simply to weak (anarchism and black hand) or
> stuff that adds an unnessary amount of luck and randomness to the game
> (gehenna events)

I'll save Eric the trouble of pointing out that Anarchs are looking
increasingly stronger now that Gehenna has given them new and powerful
options. Fortitude bleed-reduce, anyone? How about some Presence-based
stealth?

Black Hand just became much more useful since it's one of the very few
ways to counter Events. At least, that's assuming Events are as
terrifyingly game-breaking powerful as some people are claiming.

> vampires with a capacity above 8 are most of the time wallpaper
> (especially if they have no real title (bishop/primogen doesn´t count))
> there is NO benefit in playing larger vampires except if the have cool
> specials and disciplines (like the ic´s or laz).

Of course, big vampires are much more likely to have 'cool
disciplines', since they've often got so many levels of them. And I
think WW has been much better about making the bigger vamps more
interesting lately - I don't think there are that many big vamps from
any of the recent sets that are so without redeemable qualities as to
be 'wallpaper'. Most of the 'wallpaper' big vamps I hear people talk
about are actually Jyhad-set ones.

> some changes have been proposed (i suggest to LSJ at the ec that the
> biggies might need some sort of supersuperior (playable by vampires with
> a capacity above 7/8 if they have no title), just to be told that large
> vampires are strong enough)
> maybe vampires should only be allowed to bleed to a maximum of half
> their capacity
> maybe vampires should get +1 strengh when in combat with a younger vampire

You could always try to play with a few of these rules and see how it
affects game play and then tell us all your results. At least some of
these are similar to game variants that WotC published in their Jyhad
guidebook many years ago (forget the name). Things like base bleed or
strength or both increasing with the capacity of the vampire, for
instance. I seem to recall those sorts of variants falling under the
category of 'things that make games go a whoooole lot faster', too.

> a lot of people are pissed the way the bloodlones are treated (no more
> group 2 vamps, some of them totally unplayable) the average CCG player
> DOESN`T care how many samedi are found in the world of darkness!

Then those people should take some comfort from LSJ declaring in the
Developer chat that more Bloodlines vamps could well appear in future
expansions.

As to 'some of them are totally unplayable', to the best of my
knowledge there was _never_ any sort of statement that the Bloodlines
were ever intended to be playable as full standalones clans, nor even
necessarily close, and many repeated official statements to the
contrary.

The fact that some of them have turned out to be just fine on their
own (like the Ahrimanes, for instance) is nothing more than good
fortune to those Bloodlines.

(That said, it's unfortunate that a couple of them are not
particularly playable even as secondary part of a deck. !Salubri,
anyone? Anyone?)

> i appreciate that WW has been carefull about not destroying the game,
> but the stasis the game is currently in might destroy the game.
> please no flames as a reply

Without flaming you, I find it very hard to take a comment like 'the
stasis the game is currently in might destroy the game' seriously when
there are dozens and dozens of recent posters talking about how the
game has changed _too much_ with Gehenna and that the game environment
might be destroyed as a result.

> stefan

-John Flournoy

Well, I think it's way too soon to say anything about how the Event cards
will affect real play. There have been lots of cards in previous sets that
everyone was in an uproar about, when in practice they have proved to be
quite balanced. Of course, there have also been unbalanced cards and
combos. Time will tell where the Event cards fall. I sort of like them
myself.

As for stealth-bleed, yeah, I sort of agree. Having run N+1 tournaments over
here, it's still *very* rare to find a deck at the final round which
doesn't have Dominate. Bleed bounce + bleed modifiers are so powerful that
everyone and their dog plays them. Boring. One of the only exceptions are
the Anarch Revolt decks, which are even more cheesy (the day thay Anarch
Revolt gets errata I will be very happy, it's one of the more broken cards
in the game currently). But I digress.

But overall I'm pretty happy with the direction the game has taken. On my
personal wish list are:

- An errata to Anarch Revolt (make it unique, make it cost X=# of ARs
previously in play, anything). In a dedicated Master card deck with tons of
Minion Tap and Golconda, this card makes for an almost unstoppable deck
that totally circumvents the normal game mechanics (no actions, nothing to
block) and requires a whole table united from the first round to stop it.
Seen it all too many times. If you think AR is ok, you've never seen one of
these monsters play 3 ARs per round and bloat around 10 pool per round.

- Some usable way to fight against bleed bounce without playing bleed bounce
yourself. A deck without bleed bounce usually drops quickly in tournaments.

//Petri

Did you guys read the May Anarch newsletter? I think I've made a

> The randomness of some Gehenna events is very bothersome, and quite

Bah, this game has always included elements of pure luck, like table
seating. And we've always had plenty of effects that do not
discriminate between friend and foe. Someone else has said something
along these lines, but I want to push it a little farther - If you
play a Gehenna Event (or Anarch Revolt, Judgement:Camarilla
Segregation, Autarkis Persecution, etc.) that hurts your prey and/or
predator the most, you have played well. If it hurts your grandprey
the most, you have played poorly. If it manages by some miracle to
hose everyone but you and you get the sweep, you have played VERY
well. If it manages to hose everybody but your prey, then you have
played VERY poorly.

Global effects require skill. They always have. Events are no
different, and though we may see some initial spike in their use,
ultimately I think they'll have very little effect - either positive
or negative - on poor play. Poor play will always exist, and how well
you deal with it is part of what makes a really great player. It's
really just another vehicle for poor play, so it will necessarily keep
the great players on their toes. I just can't bring myself to feel
bad about that.

I understand your point, but I still disagree with it.

Without itemizing every single event, such events are only
_potentially_ game crippling to all players - depending on what their
deck does. For instance, when I play my all-Nosferatu-Anti deck, Fall
of the Camarilla does not in any way shape or form cripple my game.
Recalled to the Founder cannot ruin my 6-clan Nec/Dom/Aus deck because
I cannot have 3 of a clan in play. My Inner Circle/Justicar deck
doesn't even notice Nightmares Upon Nightmares entering play unless
there are 8 more events on the table.

Most Events are _only_ 'game-crippling to ALL players' (emphasis
yours) if every player happens to be playing the style of deck that
gets hurt by it. Otherwise, my commentary about choosing whether to
play events that potentially screw somebody across-table without
hurting your prey or predator still apply.

If there was an Event that would _always_ cripple the game of all the
players, then that would mean there was no deck that would be able to
ignore the consequences of that Event.. which means nobody would
_play_ that event, because all the Events also affect the person
playing them and they'd be just as crippled as the rest. None of them
are 'everybody but you has this effect happen'.

Keep in mind that there have already been, for years and years, cards
that you can play that hose people based on what type deck they are
playing. Judgement: Camarilla Segregation is a fine example. If I put
J:CS in play (especially if I play more than one), I could certainly
be crippling the game of anybody playing non-Cam no matter where they
are sitting.

And I'd probably be called a total idiot if I did so when the only
person playing non-Cam was my grand-prey, regardless of 'casual game'
or 'tournament game'.

Let's say that you bring a deck that's designed to play Fall of the
Camarilla, because you think that's fun. If your prey and predator are
both playing non-Camarilla decks and the two Cam vote decks are
cross-table, and you still play FotC, you are not randomly
destabilizing a table, you are _deliberately_ destabilizing it.
Because there is not a single Event that says 'YOU MUST PLAY THIS
EVENT IF YOU HAVE IT' or anything of the sort.

> Now, the second important thing to remember about my statement that
> Gehenna will cause people to leave playgroups is this: Though they
> (gehenna events) may not see tournament play (because of the rather
> random destabalizing effects they have) we WILL be seeing them in
> casual play. These cards will wreck CASUAL play, hurting our playgroup
> (as casual play we play to win AND to have fun... confusing that,
> isn't it?).

Again, the destabilizing effects are only random _if you let them be_.
By the time enough events are on the table to play Fall of the X (for
instance), you should be able to look at the table and have a pretty
damn good idea who that Event will hinder and who will ignore it.

Since there is no mandatory play of an Event, the decision to play one
is no more randomly destabilizing than any of the other cards that
impact everybody at the table - unless you are deliberately choosing
to play the event before you have any information about who that play
will affect.

If a player is indiscriminately playing cards (events or otherwise)
that might ruin a random player's game, without having any information
as to what the consequences will be, and they do so game after game,
the rest of the play group either needs to convince this player to
stop doing that, stop playing with that player, or change their
expectations of the game from 'we're going to win' to 'we're playing
totally for fun'.

Despite everything I've said, I'm sure a _lot_ of groups are going to
see events played 'for fun' in indiscriminate fashion for the next few
weeks. Cause the cards are new, and interesting, and people want to
try them out, even if that means unbalancing games randomly. But
again, this isn't the first (or second, or third, etc) time that new
cards have been released that can totally shaft somebody cross-table
when they're put into play. When the novelty of those previous cards
wore off, people stopped playing them 'just to play them' and started
making intelligent decisions (or at least trying to, heh) about how
and when to use them. I don't see how the potentially game-screwing
Events are going to be any different.

> Comprends?

Yep.

> ~SV

-John Flournoy

Precisely. This is not theoretical, I've seen these things win tournaments
over here. I'm not saying it's trivial to build a deck that really works,
but once it's done it does become a bit of a problem. Why? Because it
almost totally circumvents the normal game mechanics. Basically, all it
does is play Masters, tons of them. No actions, rushes are met with
Obedience/Majesty. It makes sure that everyone drops in the correct order
by playing life boons, and in emergency cases calling a table-rearranging
vote.

We've talked about how to fight this type of deck over here, and so far have
drawn a pretty big blank... and we're not exactly amateurs over here.

Things that have a small chance of working:

a) Bleed him out of the game, fast. Requires a dedicated and fast (stealth)
bleeder as predator.
b) Remove the Anarch Revolts and/or prevent him playing masters. Almost
impossible to do in practice, borderline possible if everyone on the table
concentrates on removing the ARs.
c) Rush him and try to drop his vampires before he can Minion Tap + Golconda
them. Very very hard to do, due to Obedience and Majesty.
d) Bloat faster than him. Almost impossible, Minion Tap + Golconda (with
Info Highway etc assisting) is very efficient.

The deck is beatable, but only in certain situations and when the whole
table suspends normal play and concentrates on ousting this one deck. The
deck consists on mostly master cards (probably 80% are masters).

I have no problems with strong decks. I do have problems with deck
archetypes that require specific anti-decks, which normal decks don't have
much of a chance against.

This is not abstract theory.

//Petri

management, not in somehow magically deciding what card will be on top

when you want to shut down everyone else's discipline-based powers,

with global effects means you must be particularly skilled in these
aspects of the game, nothing else. Otherwise such effects will make
you lose 9 times out of 10.
